20953.text: For a given curve y=2 x-x^2 , when x increases at the rate of 3 units/sec, then how does the slope of the curve change?
20953.sol: The equation of the curve is given by y = 2x - x^2 . The slope of the curve at any point x is given by m = dy dx = 2 - 2x . To find the rate of change of the slope with respect to time t , we differentiate m with respect to t using the chain rule: dm dt = d dt (2 - 2x) = -2 dx dt . Given that the rate of increase of x is dx dt = 3 units/sec, we substitute this value into the expression: dm dt = -2 3 = -6 units/sec. The negative sign indicates that the slope is decreasing at a rate of 6 units/sec. Answer: Decreasing

28479.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is Al > Mg > Mg ²⁺> Al ³⁺ . Statement II : The correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is Cl > Br > S > O . options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
28479.sol: Analyzing Statement I: The order given is Al > Mg > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺. However, the correct atomic radii order should be Mg > Al because Mg is in group 2 (period 3) while Al is in group 13 (period 3), and moving right across a period decreases radius. The correct order would be Mg > Al > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺. Therefore, Statement I is FALSE. Analyzing Statement II: Electron gain enthalpy magnitudes follow: Cl (highest, ~349 kJ/mol) > Br (~325) > S (~200) > O (~141). This is because Cl has the highest tendency to gain an electron

29235.subject: Chemistry
29235.text: The colour of K M n O 4 is due to: [where M → metal, L → ligand]
29235.sol: Charge transfer from O 2 - to empty d -orbitals of metal ion (Mn 7 + ) . The colour in KMnO 4 arises from an electronic transition. In the permanganate ion (MnO 4 − ), manganese is in the + 7 oxidation state, so it has no d electrons. Photons promote an electron from the highest energy molecular orbital to an empty d -orbital on the manganese. When a photon of light is absorbed, this charge transfer takes place from L to M .

options: They form a complex with washing soda.
109905.sol: When calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with washing soda, they form insoluble carbonates, which can be precipitated and removed.

110284.subject: Chemistry
110284.text: Which group of elements exhibits similar behavior in terms of low melting and boiling points as alkali metals?
110284.sol: Noble gases also have low melting and boiling points, similar to alkali metals, due to weak van der Waals forces between their atoms.

110390.subject: Chemistry
110390.text: Which of the following nitrates crystallizes as an anhydrous salt?
110390.sol: Barium nitrate crystallizes as the anhydrous salt, which means it does not have associated water molecules in its crystal structure.

110453.subject: Chemistry
110453.text: Why are the fluorides of alkaline earth metals relatively less soluble than the chlorides?
options: Due to their lower lattice energies
Due to their higher lattice energies
110453.sol: The fluorides of alkaline earth metals are relatively less soluble than the chlorides because they have higher lattice energies.

Due to the presence of a double bond.
Due to the higher oxidation state of oxygen.
Due to the presence of an unstable O-O bond.

111309.sol: Berthelot synthesized methane in 1856, confirming the synthesis of organic compounds from inorganic sources.

It delays the attainment of equilibrium
It has no effect on the attainment of equilibrium
It shifts the equilibrium to the left
114698.sol: A catalyst catalyzes both the forward and backward reactions to the same extent, helping the reaction reach equilibrium faster.

119267.text: An organic compound X ( C ₉ H ₁₀ O ) gives a red-orange precipitate with 2,4 -DNP reagent and a yellow precipitate upon heating with iodine and aqueous NaOH . Drastic oxidation of X with alkaline KMnO ₄ followed by acidification yields a dicarboxylic acid Y. Upon heating, compound Y readily loses a molecule of water to produce an anhydride Z. The compound X is:
119267.sol: Compound X ( C ₉ H ₁₀ O ) forms a red-orange precipitate with 2,4 -DNP, indicating the presence of a carbonyl group. It gives a yellow precipitate with I ₂/ NaOH (iodoform test), confirming the presence of a methyl ketone ( - COCH ₃ ) group. Drastic oxidation of X yields a dicarboxylic acid Y, meaning there are two oxidizable side chains on the benzene ring. 119877.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): N-methylethanamide on treatment with bromine and ethanolic sodium hydroxide gives N-methylmethanamine. Reason (R): Hoffmann bromamide degradation is given only by primary amides. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
119877.sol: N-methylethanamide (C H₃ CONHCH₃ ) is a secondary amide. The Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction is a characteristic reaction of primary amides (R-CONH₂ ) only. Secondary and tertiary amides do not undergo this reaction. Therefore, N-methylethanamide will not undergo degradation with bromine and ethanolic sodium hydroxide to yield N-methylmethanamine. When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered they were moved into classes they rightly belong to. It is also possible that the asexual and vegetative stage have been given one name (and placed under deuteromycetes) and the sexualstage another (and placed under another class). Later when the linkages were established, the fungi were correctly identified and moved out of deuteromycetes. Once perfect (sexu

121786.subject: Botany
121786.text: Into what two groups are bryophytes divided?
121786.sol: Bryophytes in general are of little economic importance but some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals, birds and other animals. Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water. Mosses along with lichens are the first organisms to colonize rocks and hence, are of great ecological importance. They decompose rocks making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants. Since mo

121971.subject: Botany
121971.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The members of phaeophyceae are called brown algae because they possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. 2. Brown algae are found only in freshwater habitats 3. Food is stored as starch. 4. The vegetative cells have a pectose wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin. 5. The plant body is usually attached to the
121971.sol: The members of phaeophyceae are found primarily in marine habitats. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. Food is stored as mannitol and laminarin. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf like photosynthetic organ – the frond.

122106.subject: Botany
122106.text: Assertion : The leaves in gymosperms are welladapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. Reason: Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
122106.sol: The leaves in gymnosperms are welladapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. In conifers, the needlelike leaves reduce the surface area. Their thick cuticle and sunken stomata also help to reduce water loss. Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.

122718.subject: Botany
122718.text: What is the name given to the swollen leaf base in leguminous plants?
122718.sol: A typical leaf consists of three main parts: leaf base, petiole and lamina (Figure 5.4 a). The leaf is attached to the stem by the leaf base and may bear two lateral small leaf like structures called stipules. In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly. In some leguminous plants the leafbase may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus. The petiole help hold the blade to light. Long thin flexible petioles allow leaf blades to flutter in wind, thereby cooling the

122880.subject: Botany
122880.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: When stamens are attached to the petals, they are called epipetalous eg. Brinjal. Reason: When stamens are attached to the perianth, it is called epiphyllous as in the flowers of jasmine
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
122880.sol: When stamens are attached to the petals, they are epipetalous as in brinjal, or epiphyllous when attached to the perianth as in the flowers of lily.

122923.subject: Botany
122923.text: Pericarp Parts Descriptions A. Epicarp 1. Inner stony layer B. Mesocarp 2. Middle fleshy layer C. Endocarp 3. Outer layer of the fruit D. Pericarp 4. The collective term for all layers of the fruit wall
122923.sol: The epicarp is the outer layer, mesocarp is the middle fleshy layer, endocarp is the inner stony layer, and pericarp is the collective term for all layers.

122927.subject: Botany
122927.text: Seed Parts Descriptions A. Seed Coat 1. Scar on the seed coat through which the seed was attached to the fruit B. Radicle 2. Part of the embryo that develops into the root C. Cotyledons 3. The outermost covering of a seed with two layers D. Micropyle 4. Fleshy structures often full of reserve food materials
122927.sol: The seed coat is the outer covering with two layers; radicle develops into the root; cotyledons are fleshy and full of reserve food materials; the micropyle is the scar through which the seed was attached to the fruit.

Column I Column II (a) Axile (i) False septum formation in a unilocular ovary; Mustard (b) Parietal (ii) Single ovule attached at the ovary base; Sunflower (c) Free central (iii) Multilocular ovary with central attachment; Lemon (d) Basal (iv) Septa are completely absent; Dianthus Select the co

Parietal placentation occurs when ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary. A false septum may form, making the unilocular ovary bilocular. Example: Mustard. Thus, (b) matches (i). Free central placentation features ovules borne on a central axis with septa completely absent. Example: Dianthus. Thus, (c) matches (iv). Basal p

122984.subject: Botany
122984.text: Read the following statements regarding the androecium in different plants: (I) In China rose, stamens are united into one bunch (monadelphous). (II) In pea, stamens are united into two bundles (diadelphous). (III) In Citrus, stamens are united into more than two bundles (polyadelphous). (IV) In lily, stamens are attached to the petals (epipetalous). Choose the correct combination of statements.
122984.sol: Statement (I) is correct: In China rose, the stamens are united into a single bundle, which is termed monadelphous. Statement (II) is correct: In pea, the stamens are united into two bundles, termed diadelphous. Statement (III) is correct: In Citrus, the stamens are united into more than two bundles, termed polyadelphous. Statement (IV) is incorrect: In lily, the stamens are attached to the perianth, a condition known as epiphyllous, not epipetalous. Epipetalous condition (attachment to petals) is seen in brinjal.

123534.subject: Botany
123534.text: What is the function of the cell cycle?
options: To ensure the integrity of the genome in progeny cells
123534.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed

124233.subject: Botany
124233.text: Flagellum Structures Components A. Axoneme 1. Nine pairs of microtubules arranged in a circle B. Peripheral Doublets 2. Connects central tubules to peripheral doublets C. Central Tubules 3. Runs parallel to the long axis of the flagellum D. Radial Spokes 4. Unconnected by bridges
124233.sol: The axoneme is the core structure of the flagellum with microtubules running parallel.Peripheral doublets are the nine pairs of microtubules arranged in a circle.Central tubules are connected by radial spokes.Radial spokes connect central tubules to peripheral doublets.

124684.subject: Botany
124684.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to environment 2. Development is considered as the sum of growth, differentiation and variation 3. Difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup represent the heterophyllous development due to environment 4. The phenomenon of heterophy
124684.sol: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment (Figure 13.9). This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.

124847.subject: Botany
124847.sol: Phytochrome is chromoprotein (photosensitive, photoreceptor, blue pigment protein complex. Found in almost all flowering plants (angiosperms).

124870.subject: Botany
124870.text: What is correct about the movement of substance across the membrane in facilitated diffusion?
options: It doesn't cause transport of molecules from low concentration to high concentration.
It is a very specific transport.
124870.sol: In facilitated diffusion special proteins help move substances across membranes along the concentration gradient without expenditure of energy. Facilitated diffusion is very specific, it allows cell to select substances for uptake. It is sensitive to inhibitors which react with protein side chains.

124925.subject: Botany
124925.text: What is the primary function of the cells in the interior of thick, woody stems?
124925.sol: Each living cell in a plant is located quite close to the surface of the plant. ‘This is true for leaves’, you may ask, ‘but what about thick, woody stems and roots?’ In stems, the ‘living’ cells are organized in thin layers inside and beneath the bark. They also have openings called lenticels. The cells in the interior are dead and provide only mechanical support. Thus, most cells of a plant have at least a part of their surface in contact with air. This is also facilitated by the loose packing of parenchyma cells

125363.subject: Botany

When there are more than one, the pistils may be fused together (syncarpous) or may be free (apocarpous) Each pistil has three parts the stigma, style and ovary. 125887.subject: Botany
125887.text: What feature of the corn cob demonstrates wind pollination?
options: The large number of ovules in each ovary
The sticky nature of the pollen grains
The tassels that wave in the wind
The enclosed nature of the flowers
125887.sol: Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollinations. Wind pollination also requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents. They often possess well-exposed stamens (so that the pollens are easily dispersed into wind currents, and large often-feathery stigma to easily trap air-borne pollen grains. Wind- pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence; a familiar example is the corn cob –

126272.subject: Botany
126272.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding pollination adaptations: List-I List-II (A) Wind pollination (I) Long, ribbon-like pollen grains (B) Water pollination in Vallisneria (II) Large, feathery stigma (C) Water pollination in Zostera (III) Female flowers reach the surface of water (D) Insect pollination (IV) Sticky pollen grains and nectar Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
126272.sol: Wind-pollinated flowers have well-exposed stamens and large, feathery stigmas to easily trap air-borne pollen grains. In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the surface of water by a long stalk and pollen grains are released on to the surface of water. In Zostera, a marine seagrass, female flowers remain submerged in water and the pollen grains are long and ribbon-like. Insect-pollinated flowers are generally large, colourful, fragrant, rich in nectar, and produce sticky pollen grains. Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III

It regulates gene expression or chromosome function
It leads to certain biochemical changes in the target tissue

128397.sol: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors (present in the nucleus). If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
128655.sol: Antidiuretic hormone ( ADH ) or vasopressin is secreted from posterior pituitary gland. It is released in response to a fall in the water content of blood plasma and leads to an increase in the permeability to water of the distal and collecting tubules of the nephron. Deficiency or hyposecretion of ADH results in diabetes insipidus. Diabetes insipidus is characterised by micturating dilute urine several times a day which results in excessive thirst (polydipsia) and dehydration.

Twice the number of chromosomes and four times the amount of DNA
Four times the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
96282.sol: S-phase (synthesis phase) is the part of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, but a number of chromosome does not change. While in a gamete, DNA content in gamete = C Chromosome in gamete = N Hence, the Number of chromosome in a somatic cell will be twice than gamete while DNA content will be four times.

306511.text: For a gas at absolute temperature T , the mean square speed of its molecules is proportional to
306511.sol: The mean square speed of gas molecules is given by the square of the root mean square speed.
